tagline: Turn four raw sources into an analysis dataset that rebuilds with one command, with its provenance, its rules and an honest account of what is missing
description: Participants assemble an analysis dataset for a fictional food bank network from four sources: registrations with personal data, branch logs, a donations API and open population data. They record provenance, join with key and cardinality checks, clean Arabic and English text, dates and units, write validation rules that rerun on every build, and measure how missing data and measurement error move a headline estimate. Personal data are minimised and pseudonymised, and the dataset rebuilds from raw sources with one command.
audience: Practitioners. Graduates and early-career analysts who have completed the FN courses or passed the placement test, and analysts moving into data science.
prerequisites: FN-101 Python for Data and AI Work
FN-106 Responsible Data and AI Practice in the Kingdom
Writes SQL joins and group-by queries without assistance
Setup: a laptop CPU with uv, or Google Colab. No key, account or model is needed. Run 00_setup_check and the two-hour pre-work notebook before Day 1; see labs/README.md.

case_study.name: Ghilal Food Bank Network
case_study.summary: Ghilal Food Bank Network (شبكة غِلال لبنوك الطعام) is a fictional network of 14 branches serving the 30 districts of a fictional city, Madinat Al-Sidr. Its programmes director asks how many parcels an eligible household received per month in each district in the third quarter of 2026; participants assemble the answer from 40,000 registrations with personal data, 210,000 branch log rows, a local donations API and an open district population table. All data is synthetic and generated with a fixed seed, with planted encoding faults, duplicate and mistyped keys, gaps, unit errors and missing household sizes that each lab finds.

capstone.summary: A rebuildable dataset for one of three synthetic questions, in a public repository whose README reports row counts per step, rule results and the estimate's sensitivity to missing data; eight-minute defence with a rebuild from raw files
capstone.submission: A public GitHub repository link. The repository rebuilds the analysis dataset from the raw files of the capstone extract with one command, and holds the provenance file, the rule suite and the set-aside rows (log id, branch and reason, without the household key as typed); its README reports row counts per step, rule results and the sensitivity of the estimate to missing data. No raw personal field is committed, synthetic or not. Then an eight-minute defence with a live rebuild, in which the assessor corrupts one input file and you show which rule fails and why, and four minutes of questions.
